body.statement:
Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) be independent random self-adjoint \(d\)-dimensional matrices with \(\mathbb E X_s=0\) and \(\lambda_{\max}(X_s)\le R\) almost surely.  If \(\sigma^2=\left\|\sum_{s=1}^N\mathbb E(X_s^2)\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), then for every \(u\ge0\),
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{\lambda_{\max}\!\left(\sum_{s=1}^NX_s\right)\ge u\right\}
 \le d\exp\!\left\{-\frac{u^2}{2\sigma^2+2Ru/3}\right\}.
\]

source.locator: Theorem 1.4 (Matrix Bernstein), with the lower tail obtained by applying the same theorem to the negated summands
source.verbatim_statement: Consider a finite sequence {Xk} of independent, random, self-adjoint matrices with dimension d. Assume that each random matrix satisfies E Xk = 0 and λmax(Xk) ≤ R almost surely. Then, for all t ≥ 0, P{λmax(Σk Xk) ≥ t} ≤ d · exp(−t²/(2σ² + Rt/3)), where σ² := ‖Σk E(Xk²)‖.

attestation.note: Verified against arXiv:1004.4389v7, Theorem 1.4, p. 4; the node’s denominator 2σ²+2Ru/3 is algebraically identical to the displayed 2(σ²+Ru/3).
